answers.answer: Shuffle Factory cards and place number of players + 1 face-down on the board; return the rest unseen. Put one encounter token on each of 11 marked territories and randomly place one structure bonus tile face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts, then clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup: “number of players + 1”; “11 marked territories”; “lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.”

answers.answer: Character at home; two workers on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining home; four mechs over Faction Mat abilities; six stars by faction emblem; six cubes in black-square green boxes; four structures in matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits on bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; action token beside Player Mat; leave one-time recruit spaces empty. Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets popularity, coins, and two objectives.

You may take either, both, or neither action, but must move to a different section; only Rusviet may repeat a section. Top-row gains may pay bottom-row cost. If taking both, top precedes bottom. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full; take as much or little of exposed green-box benefits as desired. Exact bottom costs/coin benefits depend on Player Mat and upgrades.

An enemy worker alone on your structure territory controls it and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure ability; you retain it without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. Pay using resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control/resources: “enemy worker alone”; “any territories you currently control.”

answers.answer: The two normal Move selections must be different units, so one unit cannot move twice. A transported worker may subsequently move itself. Any unit can carry any number of resources; only mechs carry your workers, never your character.
answers.evidence: Move: “two different units”; carried worker may subsequently move; only mechs carry workers.

answers.answer: A Speed mech entering enemy workers only stops and cannot move again that turn; those workers immediately retreat home and leave resources. Lose one popularity per worker, but zero popularity does not stop retreat. Its workers cannot independently enter territory controlled by enemy workers.
answers.evidence: Move: enemy workers retreat, leave resources, popularity loss down to zero; worker entry restriction.

answers.answer: After all units finish moving, resolve combat before the following bottom action; attacker chooses order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Move/combat: combat after movement and before bottom action; attacker chooses order; worker restriction.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card; if deck empty shuffle discards into a new deck, and if both are empty draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity. Put traded resources on a controlled territory with at least one worker; if all workers are home, cannot Trade for resources.

Pay all exposed Produce costs in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories (before upgrades); each worker there may produce one matching terrain token there. New workers come from Player Mat left to right and go in producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Newly exposed costs apply to future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce steps and new worker/cost instructions.

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes; Deploy costs the exposed Deploy-box metal count; amounts vary by mat/upgrades. Upgrade moves a cube from green to an empty bracketed red box to improve top benefit/reduce bottom cost; solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy places a mech on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake; its ability applies to character and every mech, not workers. Even with all pieces completed, pay a bottom action for coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.

Build on a controlled territory with your worker, at most one structure total per territory; Factory allowed, lakes/home bases forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. You retain structure abilities when enemies occupy the territory, but Mill only produces while you control it. Mine remains your personal movement tunnel even when enemy-controlled; opponents cannot use its ability.

Take a recruit from any bottom-row section and permanently place it on any open one-time Faction Mat bonus: two power, coins, popularity, or combat cards. Ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where recruit was removed. Resolve qualifying bonuses active player, then left neighbor, then right; stop if sixth star ends game. In two-player play opponent triggers once.

Each combatant simultaneously and secretly chooses dial power from 0 to min(7, current power), then may add one combat card per participating character/mech; Rusviet People's Army adds one card total if workers present; workers alone do not fight. Reveal together; add values and attacker wins ties. If both have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Both deduct dial power and discard all cards face-up; card values do not deduct track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–4 and mech ability order.

answers.answer: Winner controls territory/resources and places combat star if eligible (ordinarily max two; Saxony unrestricted within six). All losing characters, mechs, workers retreat home, leaving resources; Seaworthy can retreat eligible units/carried workers to adjacent lakes. Winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by defeated mech on a lake; defender loses none, except Polania Camaraderie rule. Loser draws one combat card if revealed at least one power on dial or through cards; zero-total loser gets none.

After whole Move action and all combats, resolve encounter only if character remains; if it loses contested entry, it retreats and token stays. Gains go to encounter territory. Pay printed option cost but no normal action cost or mat benefits/ongoing recruit bonuses apply.

Every player's character chooses one available Factory card on its first finish of Move there (after winning combat if needed); later visits cannot exchange it and each player gets at most one. Use as fifth action section, optional top then bottom, usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception); no corresponding mat coins, structure bonuses or recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories, or three for Speed character/mech, with normal restrictions and Mine access.

Reveal completed objective only on own turn, before or after top/bottom action, meeting all requirements at reveal. Place star and put both objective cards at bottom of deck. Normally one objective star; Saxony keeps second card after first and may score both.

Stars for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two ordinarily), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each once except two combat stars and Saxony exception; others' stars do not block. Placed stars are permanent if power/popularity drops. Sixth star immediately ends play.

For a bottom-row sixth star, finish the action and collect primary benefit, coins and active player's ongoing recruit benefit before placing star. Resolve eligible recruit bonuses/stars active, then left, then right, stopping at sixth star. If units remain in unresolved battle, undo that part of movement and do not resolve another combat.
answers.evidence: Immediate end: bottom action sequence and pending battle.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, five stars score $20 ($4 each). Four normal territories plus Factory count as 7 territories; at $3 each that is $21. Thirteen resources make six pairs; at $2 per pair that is $12. These add $53 to held coins, plus selected structure bonus (amount depends on tile/features). Ties break by workers + mechs + structures, power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, stars placed.
answers.evidence: Scoring tables: popularity 7–12; Factory counts 3; pairs; structure tile; tiebreakers. Held coins and structure tile outcome unspecified.

answers.answer: Home base is not a territory and normally cannot be entered; setup/forced retreats are exceptions, as is unlocked Crimea Wayfare. Bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.

Mountain produces metal, tundra oil, farm food, forest wood, village a worker; lake and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.

Any unit may pick up/carry/drop any number of resources mid-movement; only mechs carry workers, never your character. Speed adds one territory to each selected character/mech, not workers; tunnel jump costs one step and extra step may be before/after. Enemy-unit and encounter stops override Speed.
Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure and take control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
Do not pay partial Produce cost. If unable to afford any action, move token to a different section and take neither action (dead turn).
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: full costs and dead turn.

answers.answer: Armory grants one power on Trade; Monument one popularity on Bolster. You retain structure abilities without control despite enemy occupant, except Mill production requires control.

Riverwalk for character/mechs: Rusviet farms/villages; Crimea farms/tundra; Nordic forests/mountains; Polania villages/mountains; Saxony forests/mountains. Nordic Swim lets workers cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes, and does not help character/mechs or provide lake movement.

Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels, including its Mine, adjacent for character/mech Move. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and Factory adjacent for character/mech Move.

Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or its Mine: opponent loses two power on track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery instead lets you pay one power before combat to reduce opponent's power by two, once per combat, not per unit.

People's Army allows one additional combat card total when at least one worker is present. Two mechs and three workers allow three cards. Workers alone never fight; a character or mech is still required.
Crimea Wayfare moves character/mechs from a territory or home base to own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases; not an active opponent base.
Scout steals one random opponent combat card into your hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion spends one combat card once per turn as any one resource, regardless of card value.

Seaworthy allows character/mechs to move to/from lakes and retreat to adjacent lake. Submerge allows character/mechs to move to/from lakes and between any lakes, but no adjacent-lake retreat exception. Workers on lakes need a mech to move off; carried workers/resources cannot be left behind on a lake when carrier leaves.
Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins combat as aggressor on its turn; it does not cover driving off undefended workers without combat.
Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; pay each printed cost and first gain may pay second cost. May take as little of benefits as desired.
A character reaching an encounter during Factory Move stops and cannot move again that turn. Resolve encounter after entire Move action and all combats, if character remains.

Coins are not hidden, but exact total need not be disclosed on request. Combat card hand count is public, but during combat may conceal whether cards were committed until reveal; contents secret until reveal. Objective contents secret until completed objective is revealed.

Only coins are tangible exchangeable items; agreements informal and unenforceable (tournament forbids even coin deal exchanges). Payment/negotiation cannot cancel combat once movement initiated it; combat proceeds after Move, though bribes may influence result.

At popularity 0–6 score $3/star, $2/territory, $1/pair; 7–12: $4/$3/$2; 13–18: $5/$4/$3. Controlled lakes count one; Factory counts three; home bases do not. Only complete resource pairs score; odd leftovers ignored.

Adjacency bonuses count unique printed features across all structures; rivers do not break adjacency. Tunnel tile excludes Mines; lake tile counts unique lakes; encounter tile counts unique printed encounter locations even if token removed. Tunnels: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6=$9; lakes and encounters: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6–7=$9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table and adjacency rules.

answers.answer: Structures on printed tunnel territories (not Mines): 1=$2, 2=$4, 3–4=$6. In a row counts only longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break line; 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9. Farms/tundras count combined: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9.
Yes. Winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by defeated mech on lake, subject to Polania Camaraderie exception.
A placed popularity star is permanent but does not protect current popularity; current popularity determines final scoring. Other players' stars never block a faction from achieving the same goal.

Randomly deal each player a Faction Mat and Player Mat. Seat factions clockwise in order Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. Immediate left/right neighbors trigger recruit bonuses, so seating determines which players trigger yours.

A river is a border between two land territories; a lake fills an entire hex and extends to adjacent shorelines. A unit with lake movement may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
No. Show drawn encounter card to all players, show artwork, read capitalized thematic text aloud; options need not all be read aloud.
No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
Next clockwise player may begin after current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure, or recruit to gain.
Normally no: each section's top and bottom actions are each optional and taken at most once. Rusviet may repeat a section, including Factory.
If you do not move units, normal unupgraded Move lets you gain $1.
No. Workers never return to Player Mat, including after retreat; new workers come from Player Mat left to right during Produce.
Yes. You may attack with zero power and zero popularity.
Yes, you may continue to fight after reaching combat-star limit; ordinary faction simply cannot place more than two combat stars.
Without Meander, must choose one affordable option; cannot decline all or choose unaffordable coin/popularity option. May take as little of chosen benefit as desired.
No turn-order sequence: both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose dials and optional cards, then reveal simultaneously.
Announce bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.

Place a star as soon as its goal is achieved; sixth star immediately ends play, so it cannot be delayed/declined. A completed objective may be held and revealed later, but requirements must all be met at reveal.
Ordinarily no: units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes; abilities provide exceptions.
No. Enlisted recruit is permanently placed on an open one-time Faction Mat bonus and cannot later move.
No. Only character triggers an encounter; mech/worker entering does not resolve or remove token.

Controlled Mill adds one production territory: normal two become up to three, upgraded three becomes up to four. Mill counts as one producing worker even with no actual worker there; actual workers there also produce, adding their output to Mill's. Mill product follows terrain table.

Control is established by your unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish control; if your last unit leaves and there is no qualifying structure, resources do not preserve control.
Build costs wood; Enlist costs food.
